content.comment_body: Hello! I’d like to be able to enter and show negative values on a [company_name] HMI panel for use in a [product_name] controller, version [version_no]. For example, I need to start a heating coil at -4°C (or any chosen value), and display current temperature, which could be as low as -30°C. Is this possible? As far as I know, [product_name] only uses Word as a variable type. I’m new to this.
In the tag table within [product_name] engineering software, use the Int data type instead of Word.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is having trouble displaying and entering negative temperature values, such as -4°C or -30°C, on an HMI panel connected to a [product_name] controller. They’re uncertain if the controller accepts negative numbers, since only Word appears as a variable type. Feedback from the community clarifies the need to select the Int data type, pointing out a common issue for newcomers who may not be familiar with variable types and data handling.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to easily input and show negative temperature values through the HMI panel and have these processed correctly by the [product_name] controller.
